implementation.argument_surface: receiver in ECX; no ordinary stack arguments
implementation.body: Forms the byte address receiver+4 (ADD EAX,0x4), takes the dword at that address plus 4 (the dword at receiver+8), pre-increments it, stores the incremented value back, and returns it: observationally 'return ++*(uint32_t*)((char*)self + 8);'. The machine reads the field dword twice, both reads before the store; the double read is a -O0 artifact and the single-read pre-increment is observationally identical.

observed_original_abi.receiver_basis: vftable slot membership (rule V1-VFT), not a body read. 0x0051e340 is the value of a slot in 42 vptr-backed vftables (predicate P over the PE image); the callee pops nothing and no stack word is read as an argument, so the receiver is not in the callee-popped area, and of __thiscall/__fastcall only ECX carries one. The body itself spills ECX and later reassigns it, so the convention is a statement about how the slot is reached, not something the body's bytes discriminate.
observed_original_abi.callee_saved_pushes: PUSH EBP only (the frame pointer, restored by POP EBP; EBP is not an argument)
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: integral_in_EAX at 32-bit width; the engine's own classifier says pointer_like because the last EAX write is a load from memory, which is the conservative reading of the same fact
observed_original_abi.return_type_rationale: The last definition of EAX before the RET is MOV EAX,dword ptr [EBP + -0xc], a full 32-bit load of the spilled old+1 value, so all four bytes of the result are defined and the width is 4. The value is the pre-incremented field dword, so std::uint32_t is the width-computable builtin true of the listing; the engine's return record names register EAX and leaves type null, and its register_class is pointer_like only because a value loaded from memory cannot be distinguished from a pointer by the classifier. The width is the machine fact; the spelling is the source-side choice among 4-byte types.
observed_original_abi.tail_call: absent. The body contains no JMP and no CALL; the only control transfer is the terminal RET at 0x0051e373.

conclusions: 0x0051e340 is a virtual member of some class, never of one named class: 42 vptr-backed tables hold it, which is ICF collapse, and no rule can attribute it to a single class.
The adjacent slot holds 0x0051e380 in every table read, so the two bodies are sibling virtuals of one family; 0x0051e380 is the obvious next target.

mechanics.shape: straight-line: no branch, no call, no jump, no indirect transfer. The only control transfer is the terminal RET.
mechanics.receiver_dependence: the body reads the receiver only to form the byte address receiver+4; the value it acts on is the dword at receiver+8.
mechanics.memory_effects: one dword read twice and written once, all at receiver+8; the dword at receiver+4 is computed as an address and never dereferenced as data; the frame holds three locals ([EBP-0x8] the spilled receiver, [EBP-0x4] the derived address, [EBP-0xc] the spilled result).
mechanics.globals: none. The listing names no data-segment address, and the body reaches memory only through the receiver and its own frame.
mechanics.indirect_transfers: none. The body loads nothing through a pointer with the intent to transfer control; it performs no virtual dispatch of its own -- although it IS itself the target of virtual dispatch (a slot in 42 tables).
mechanics.direct_transfers: none. No CALL or JMP with an immediate operand exists in the body, so there is no statically-named callee. This is consistent with the briefing's empty callees and callers lists, which is a property of the code rather than a gap in the evidence.
mechanics.callers: none by direct call. The only reachability is the virtual dispatch through the 42 slots, whose call sites are data references and are therefore not enumerable as code callers.

return_semantics.basis: the last definition of EAX before the RET is a full 32-bit load of the spilled old+1 value, so the result is a defined 32-bit quantity on the only path.
return_semantics.ownership: pure. The body allocates nothing, acquires and releases nothing, and mutates only the one receiver dword it is about.

direct_transfers.note: the only control transfer in the body is the terminal RET at 0x0051e373

unresolved_questions: The class is unknown and unknowable from this evidence: 42 vptr-backed tables hold the body, which is ICF collapse, so 'virtual member of some class' is the strongest true statement.

Which member sits at receiver+8 is not established. The offset is a composition of two machine displacements; the member's name, type and purpose (a counter? a version? an index?) are not recoverable from a 20-instruction body that only increments it.

The machine reads the field dword twice, both reads before the store. The source spells a single-read pre-increment, which is observationally identical because nothing runs between the reads; whether the original source was '++x', 'x = x + 1' or 'return x++ + 1' cannot be decided from the bytes.

The engine's return classifier says pointer_like (the last EAX write is a load from memory) while the source reads the value as an integral dword. The width (4 bytes) is the machine fact both agree on; the classification difference is recorded rather than resolved.

The receiver-relative offset 0x8 is not machine-attested as a single operand: the machine states 0x4 twice. A runtime trace of a constructed object would settle the layout, but no original-process trace exists in this repository.
